First, we rewrite the polynomial, interpreting any constants as multiples of the identity matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(X) & ={X}^{2}+X+2 \\  & ={X}^{2}+X+2I\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find $f(H)={H}^{2}+H+2I.$

Let's calculate ${H}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}^{2} & =H\cdot H \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}22 & 4 \\ -12 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can evaluate $f(H):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(H) & ={H}^{2}+H+2I \\  & =[\begin{aligned}22 & 4 \\ -12 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}22 & 4 \\ -12 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}5 & 1 \\ -3 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}22+5+2 & 4+1+0 \\ -12-3+0 & -2-1+2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}29 & 5 \\ -15 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
